question_text: What is the difference between a binary semaphore and a reentrant mutex?

options.text: A mutex has ownership semantics and can only be unlocked by the thread that locked it; a semaphore can be signaled by any thread
Semaphores cannot be used across processes
Mutexes permit arbitrary thread counts simultaneously
Binary semaphores are implemented exclusively in user space

answer_explanation: Mutexes embody ownership: only the acquiring thread may release the lock. Semaphores are signaling mechanisms without ownership, allowing thread A to signal thread B.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: A. Rationale: Mutexes embody ownership: only the acquiring thread may release the lock. Semaphores are signaling mechanisms without ownership, allowing thread A to signal thread B.
